properties.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
properties.digitization_method: SPLIT 2026-09-16 from the combined blklot 4046001 row (see Building 101's digitization_method for the full context). Matched using Figure 6.4.2's own '104' label position, transformed via this site's validated 6-point affine transform, matched to the nearest real footprint (39.2m away, clearly the best match) -- confirmed by direct visual overlay showing this footprint sitting right under the diagram's '104' box. This is a REAL surveyed building outline, not a diagram trace.
properties.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 104. Buildings 122 and 123 (two small one-story 'check house' buildings flanking Building 104, per the 2013 HPC packet -- 774 GSF and 400 GSF respectively) are NOT separately represented here or anywhere else in this dataset: no footprint of a matching small size was found immediately adjacent to this one, most likely because DataSF's building-footprint extraction merged them into this building's outline (or Building 102's) given how small and closely attached they are. Their combined ~1,174 GSF (~109 m2) is a small fraction of this footprint's ~1,080 m2 total, so if merged in, they would not meaningfully distort this shape -- but their own individual positions are not confirmed and are not claimed here.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: This parcel (blklot 4046001) has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll. The real Assessor lot groups 5 named buildings into one polygon with no further official subdivision -- this feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
properties.regulatory_context: UIW (Union Iron Works) Headquarters, Building 104, a Renaissance Revival structure built in 1896 with a distinctive clerestory top floor, unreinforced masonry construction. Per the 2013 HPC packet (2013.1168E), it was previously used as a naval hospital/medical office (WWII-era conversion) and was a 'red-tagged,' seismically challenged building at review time; rehab included demolishing demising walls from the WWII conversion. Part of the same 20th Street Historic Core rehabilitation by Orton Development Inc. as Buildings 101/102. ~30,000 sf usable (likely gross floor area across multiple levels, not this footprint's own area). Now houses a confidential corporate office tenant, 300+ employees.
properties.notes: Split 2026-09-16 from the combined 'Historic Core, north side' entry -- see accuracy_caveat re: Buildings 122/123.
